name.hi: एक से अधिक विधियों का उपयोग
name.en: Using More Than One Separation Method

hi.concept: मिश्रणों में मौजूद घटकों को उनके गुणों में अंतर के आधार पर अलग किया जा सकता है। इस अध्याय में हस्तचयन, थ्रेशिंग, ओसाई, चालनी, अवसादन, निस्तारण, निस्यंदन, वाष्पीकरण और संघनन जैसी विधियों को समझाया गया है। कुछ मिश्रणों के लिए एक से अधिक विधियों को क्रम से उपयोग करना पड़ता है। संतृप्त विलयन में निश्चित तापमान पर और विलेय नहीं घुल सकता।
hi.example: चावल से पत्थर चुनना, गेहूँ से दाने निकालना, भूसी को ओसाई से अलग करना, चाय को छानना और नमक के घोल से वाष्पीकरण द्वारा नमक प्राप्त करना रोजमर्रा के पृथक्करण के उदाहरण हैं।
keyPoints: मिश्रण के घटकों को अलग करने के लिए उनके गुणों में अंतर उपयोगी होता है।
हस्तचयन में अवांछित घटक हाथ से चुने जाते हैं।
थ्रेशिंग में अनाज डंठलों से अलग किया जाता है।
ओसाई हल्के और भारी घटकों के अंतर का उपयोग करती है।
चालनी कणों के आकार में अंतर का उपयोग करती है।
अवसादन में भारी अघुलनशील कण नीचे बैठते हैं।
निस्तारण में ऊपर का द्रव अलग किया जाता है और निस्यंदन में फिल्टर उपयोगी होता है।
वाष्पीकरण द्रव को वाष्प में बदलता है और संघनन वाष्प को द्रव में बदलता है।
कुछ मिश्रणों में एक से अधिक पृथक्करण विधियों का क्रम से उपयोग किया जाता है।

examTraps.title: ओसाई बनाम चालनी
examTraps.fact: ओसाई में हवा और चालनी में छिद्रों का उपयोग होता है।
examTraps.confusion: दोनों को केवल ठोसों की विधि मानकर उनका आधार एक जैसा न समझें।

examTraps.title: अवसादन बनाम निस्तारण
examTraps.fact: अवसादन में कण नीचे बैठते हैं और निस्तारण में ऊपर का द्रव अलग किया जाता है।
examTraps.confusion: दोनों प्रक्रियाओं को एक ही चरण न मानें।

examTraps.title: निस्यंदन और घुला नमक
examTraps.fact: सामान्य निस्यंदन घुले हुए नमक को पानी से अलग नहीं करता।
examTraps.confusion: फिल्टर को हर प्रकार के ठोस को रोकने वाला न समझें।

examTraps.title: वाष्पीकरण बनाम संघनन
examTraps.fact: वाष्पीकरण द्रव से वाष्प और संघनन वाष्प से द्रव का परिवर्तन है।
examTraps.confusion: दोनों अवस्थाओं की दिशा उलटी होती है।

examTraps.title: संतृप्त विलयन
examTraps.fact: संतृप्त विलयन में निश्चित तापमान पर और विलेय नहीं घुलता।
examTraps.confusion: संतृप्त का अर्थ यह नहीं कि विलयन में विलेय नहीं है।

examTraps.title: थ्रेशिंग बनाम ओसाई
examTraps.fact: थ्रेशिंग अनाज को डंठल से अलग करती है और ओसाई हल्की भूसी को भारी अनाज से अलग करती है।
examTraps.confusion: कटाई के बाद दोनों विधियों का क्रम याद रखें।

sections.title: पृथक्करण की आवश्यकता
sections.concept: मिश्रण के घटकों को अलग करने की आवश्यकता इसलिए पड़ती है क्योंकि हमें अनुपयोगी या हानिकारक पदार्थ हटाने, उपयोगी घटक प्राप्त करने और अधिक शुद्ध नमूना पाने की जरूरत होती है।
sections.explanation: मिश्रण के घटकों को अलग करने की आवश्यकता इसलिए पड़ती है क्योंकि हमें अनुपयोगी या हानिकारक पदार्थ हटाने, उपयोगी घटक प्राप्त करने और अधिक शुद्ध नमूना पाने की जरूरत होती है।

en.concept: Components in a mixture can be separated by using differences in their properties. This chapter explains handpicking, threshing, winnowing, sieving, sedimentation, decantation, filtration, evaporation and condensation. Some mixtures require more than one method in sequence. In a saturated solution, no more solute can dissolve at a given temperature.
en.example: Picking stones from rice, releasing grains from wheat stalks, separating husk by winnowing, straining tea and obtaining salt by evaporation are everyday examples of separation.
keyPoints: Differences in component properties are useful for separation.
Handpicking removes unwanted components by hand.
Threshing separates grains from stalks.
Winnowing uses the difference between lighter and heavier components.
Sieving uses differences in particle size.
In sedimentation, heavier insoluble particles settle.
In decantation the upper liquid is separated, while filtration uses a filter.
Evaporation changes liquid to vapour and condensation changes vapour to liquid.
Some mixtures require more than one separation method in sequence.
examFocus: Sequence of sedimentation, decantation and filtration
State changes in evaporation and condensation
Correct sequence using more than one separation method
Choosing a method from component properties

examTraps.title: Winnowing versus sieving
examTraps.fact: Winnowing uses air while sieving uses sieve holes.
examTraps.confusion: Do not treat their separation basis as identical just because both can separate solids.

examTraps.title: Sedimentation versus decantation
examTraps.fact: Particles settle during sedimentation and the upper liquid is separated during decantation.
examTraps.confusion: Do not treat both as the same step.

examTraps.title: Filtration and dissolved salt
examTraps.fact: Ordinary filtration does not separate dissolved salt from water.
examTraps.confusion: Do not assume a filter retains every kind of solid.

examTraps.title: Evaporation versus condensation
examTraps.fact: Evaporation changes liquid to vapour while condensation changes vapour to liquid.
examTraps.confusion: The direction of the state change is opposite.

examTraps.title: Saturated solution
examTraps.fact: At a given temperature, a saturated solution cannot dissolve more solute.
examTraps.confusion: Saturated does not mean that no solute is present.

examTraps.title: Threshing versus winnowing
examTraps.fact: Threshing separates grain from stalks while winnowing separates light husk from heavier grain.

thinkBeforeAnswer: Are the components solids or a solid and a liquid?
Which property differs between the components?
Can a visible component be picked by hand?
Can air separate light and heavy components?
Do the particles differ in size?
Will a heavy insoluble component settle?
Is a solid dissolved in a liquid?
memoryTricks: Blow the light part away → winnowing.
mustRemember: Separation → separating components of a mixture
Handpicking → removing visible unwanted components by hand
Threshing → separating grains from stalks
Winnowing → separating lighter and heavier components using air
Sieving → separating particles of different sizes
Sedimentation → settling of heavier insoluble particles
Decantation → separating the upper liquid
Filtration → separating an insoluble solid with a filter
Evaporation → liquid changes to vapour
Condensation → vapour changes to liquid
Saturated solution → no more solute dissolves at a given temperature
en.quickRevision: Mixture → differences in component properties → suitable separation → handpicking → threshing → winnowing → sieving → sedimentation → decantation → filtration → evaporation → condensation → saturated solution → more than one method when needed.

sections.title: Need for Separation
sections.concept: We separate components of mixtures to remove unwanted or harmful materials, obtain useful components and get purer samples.
sections.explanation: We separate components of mixtures to remove unwanted or harmful materials, obtain useful components and get purer samples.
sections.example: Removing stones from rice is an example of removing an unwanted component.
keyPoints: Removing unwanted components
Removing harmful components
Obtaining useful components
Obtaining a purer sample
Separation uses differences in component properties

sections.title: Handpicking and Threshing
sections.concept: Handpicking removes visible unwanted components by hand. Threshing separates grain from the stalks of a plant.
sections.explanation: Handpicking removes visible unwanted components by hand. Threshing separates grain from the stalks of a plant.
sections.example: Picking pebbles from pulses is handpicking, while releasing grains from wheat stalks is threshing.
keyPoints: Handpicking is done by hand
The unwanted component should be clearly identifiable
Threshing separates grain and stalks
Threshing involves beating or shaking stalks
The two methods suit different mixtures

sections.title: Winnowing and Sieving
sections.concept: Winnowing uses air to separate lighter and heavier components. Sieving separates solid particles of different sizes using sieve holes.
sections.explanation: Winnowing uses air to separate lighter and heavier components. Sieving separates solid particles of different sizes using sieve holes.
sections.example: Separating light husk from grain is winnowing, while separating larger particles from flour is sieving.
keyPoints: Air is useful in winnowing
Heavier grains fall down
Light husk is carried away by air
Sieving uses differences in particle size
Larger particles may remain on the sieve

sections.title: Sedimentation, Decantation and Filtration
sections.concept: Heavier insoluble particles can settle at the bottom of a liquid; this is sedimentation. The upper liquid can then be separated by decantation. Filtration uses a filter to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid.
sections.explanation: Heavier insoluble particles can settle at the bottom of a liquid; this is sedimentation. The upper liquid can then be separated by decantation. Filtration uses a filter to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid.
sections.example: When sand and water are left undisturbed, sand settles and the upper water can be carefully separated.
keyPoints: Particles settle during sedimentation
The upper liquid is separated in decantation
A filter is useful in filtration
An insoluble solid can be separated by filtration
Dissolved salt is not separated by an ordinary filter

sections.title: Evaporation and Condensation
sections.concept: Evaporation changes a liquid into vapour, while condensation changes vapour into liquid. Evaporation can separate a dissolved solid from a liquid.
sections.explanation: Evaporation changes a liquid into vapour, while condensation changes vapour into liquid. Evaporation can separate a dissolved solid from a liquid.
sections.example: Evaporation helps obtain salt from seawater, while droplets on a cool surface illustrate condensation.
keyPoints: Evaporation changes liquid to vapour
Condensation changes vapour to liquid
Salt can be obtained from a salt solution by evaporation
Water vapour can condense on a cool surface
Drying clothes is an example of evaporation

sections.title: Saturated Solution
sections.concept: At a given temperature, a solution in which no more solute can dissolve is called saturated. The dissolving limit can change with temperature.
sections.explanation: At a given temperature, a solution in which no more solute can dissolve is called saturated. The dissolving limit can change with temperature.
sections.example: When sugar is added repeatedly to water, a point may be reached where additional sugar no longer dissolves.
keyPoints: A saturated solution contains solute
A given temperature matters
Additional solute may stop dissolving
Changing temperature can change dissolving capacity
A solute dissolves in a solvent

sections.title: Using More Than One Separation Method
sections.concept: Some mixtures require more than one separation method in sequence to obtain different components. The choice depends on component properties and the desired substance.
sections.explanation: Some mixtures require more than one separation method in sequence to obtain different components. The choice depends on component properties and the desired substance.
sections.example: For sand and salt, salt can be dissolved in water, sand filtered out and water evaporated to recover salt.
keyPoints: One mixture may need several methods
The next method can change after a first step
Different component properties guide method choice
Sand and salt may require dissolving, filtration and evaporation
The desired substance affects the final step
